messages:
maria: bringing up llama-2-70b-q4_0 on sm86-dedicated, hitting intermittent OOMs and 200-300ms tail for short replies when batch_size >= 6. config we used:
```
model: llama-2-70b-q4_0
batch_size: 6
max_new_tokens: 1024
seq_len: 4096
continuous_batching: true
max_batch_tokens: 131072
```
Anyone seen fragmentation or weird nvml spikes with sm86?

jonathan: kv-cache + batching is the usual suspect. with big seq_len the KV cache grows fast. try max_new_tokens=256 first and lower max_batch_size to 3. also add per-route token caps at the router so a single long request can't push the batch budget.

maria: lowered max_new_tokens to 256 and max_batch_size to 3. OOMs decreased but now short chats (1-2 tokens) have much worse latency — looks like the batcher waits for slower callers.

kai: can you paste worker logs + nvidia-smi? Also try setting `batcher_target_latency_ms=25` so it flushes faster, and `max_batch_size=3`. if fragmentation is the issue, `CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1` helped us.

maria: logs (trimmed):
```
[worker-1] ERROR runtime: CUDA out of memory allocating 900 MiB for KV cache
[worker-1] WARN runtime: allocator fragmentation: free_chunks=10 largest_free=980MiB
[worker-1] INFO batcher: built batch size=5 tokens=85000 latency=240ms
```

lena: q4_0 vs q4f16 tradeoffs matter here. q4f16 can increase peak temporary allocations with some fused kernels on sm86 drivers, which triggers earlier OOMs. q4_0 tends to use less peak scratch memory but sometimes lower op throughput. A quick A/B with identical traffic and an offline kernel compile helps.

olivia: fragmentation after rolling restarts showed up in our last bring-up. two mitigations that worked: enable `CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1` + restart; and run workers with jemalloc to reduce glibc fragmentation. also schedule a soft restart every 4-8h during the initial rollout to avoid long-lived fragmentation.

jonathan: plus consider changing the default `max_new_tokens` per-route: interactive endpoints -> 64-128; long-compute endpoints -> 512-1024. also think about two-tier routing: route short-response requests to a quantized low-mem variant, and long-response requests to a higher-memory variant. reduces tail latency for quick replies.

sre-bot: deploy 1714125000: scaled sm86-pool -> 6 instances :white_check_mark:

maria: plan for next run: reduce max_new_tokens->256 for general traffic, set max_batch_size->3, batcher_target_latency_ms->25, enable CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1 + jemalloc, run q4_0 vs q4f16 perf A/B with same prompt set, collect 2k eval prompts for quality/regression and perf bench. will post perf + perplexity diffs in ~3 cycles (~4h).

kai: if quality drops on q4_0, try hybrid: use q4_0 for short responses and q4f16 for generation-heavy routes, or fallback by token-budget. also instrument per-token memory and add eviction metrics for KV cache.

maria: thanks — kicking off A/B now. will share sample outputs, failure logs, and regression numbers. :thumbsup:
